about: What a pi-based coding harness gives each model, from bench results (agentbench). A rule goes in only with a measured gain; candidates without one are listed under optional.

rules.why: 2026-11-24, agentic-v4: pi's bash tool has no default timeout; one command that never ended (DeepSeek fuzzing a calculator) used a task's whole 15 minutes. Every command stops after 120 s unless the model asks for more (600 s at most).

2026-11-14, agentic-v1: Gemma 4 26B solved 0/5 and 1/5 bare, with a 15-25 min hang every run (thinking-only turns, tool calls written as text); with the guard 3/5 in three runs, 4.6 min, no hang. Gemma 4 12B: 1/5 either way. Not on for Qwen 3.8 27B (4/5 either way, the guard took no action) or gpt-oss 20B (no gain).

optional.why: Coding rules, keyword guides, a wake-up to test unverified changes. agentic-v1..v3: gpt-oss 20B 2-5/5 across ~20 setups vs 5/5 bare on v2 and v3; Qwen 3.8 27B 3-5/5 vs 4-5/5 bare: no gain shown yet.

Test yourself first, as a harness behavior for every task (asked for 2026-11-25): a change with no passing test run after it (pytest, npm test, ./check, ./fight, ...) wakes the agent to test it, plus a one-paragraph rule. Being A/B tested per kind of task in agentbench (coding, the arena gauntlet, arena analysis); not on by default until it shows a gain.
Long jobs in the background, the agent woken when they finish: a convenience, not benched.
